changeNote: Strict evidence re-audit after user-identified reliability concerns. All 240 literal questions reconsidered; unsupported representative modelling, missing doctrinal positions and permission-to-recommendation inferences withdrawn as null/unknown. Revision 1 remains immutable. Draft is not publishable until evidence gaps and independent review are resolved.

metadata.name: Anarcho-capitalism (Rothbardian)
metadata.description: Rothbardian natural-rights market anarchism, centred on For a New Liberty (1973/1978) and the property-rights tradition: voluntary protection, private provision and rejection of the state.
metadata.scope: The natural-rights market anarchism articulated in For a New Liberty and The Ethics of Liberty, distinguished from Hoppean covenant communities and consequentialist market anarchism. No incumbent government is claimed to implement this doctrine completely. Strict revision-2 re-audit: assess only source-supported positions on the exact questions. Unsupported empirical comparisons, modern technology analogies and institutional particulars remain unknown. Absence of doctrine is not a neutral position. This draft must not be used to calculate or publish a complete profile. Rothbard’s stateless ideal is not silently recast as a transitional parliamentary democracy. Where a question requires a choice between state arrangements he rejects, unresolved institutional fit is disclosed rather than interpreted as endorsement of the opposite pole.
metadata.phrase: A stateless society organising services, law and protection through voluntary contracts and private property.

sources.title: For a New Liberty: revised edition, especially chapters 2–15
